subject: business-studies
title: Payback and ARR
welcome_lead: Two quick yardsticks for screening investments.
meta_desc: A-Level Investment Appraisal: payback period and accounting rate of return.
final_note: Payback is fast and intuitive; ARR captures profitability over the life.

concepts.def: Time taken for cash inflows to repay the initial outlay.
Average annual profit divided by initial investment, times 100.
Cash spent at the start of the project.
Net profit each year from the project.
Payback prioritises getting cash back quickly.

walkthroughs.body_html: Add cumulative cash flows year by year until they equal the initial outlay. Project cost 100, inflows of 40 then 40 then 40 - payback occurs in year 3 (at 2.5 years).
ARR = average annual profit / initial investment x 100. Easy to calculate from accounts but ignores the timing of profits - a serious weakness.
Firms use payback for cash-tight contexts and risky projects, ARR for comparing profitability quickly, and NPV for serious investment decisions.

options: Average annual profit / initial investment x 100
